analysis.one_liner: Trent runs Tata Group's fashion and retail chains in India - the budget-fashion chain Zudio, the mid-premium Westside, and grocery/beauty formats like Star Bazaar and Zudio-adjacent Samoh/Misbu.
analysis.whats_happening: Trent's board meets on 29 October 2026 (about two weeks from now) to approve audited Q2 and H1 FY27 results. A preliminary business update on 6 October already showed standalone revenue up 23% YoY to ₹5,788 crore in Q2, with H1 FY27 revenue up 21% to ₹11,454 crore. Zudio crossed 1,000 stores during the quarter, taking the group's total store count to 1,342.
analysis.plain_terms: Trent looks like it's growing fast - revenue is up more than a fifth from a year ago - but the growth is increasingly coming from opening new stores rather than existing stores selling more. Brokerage estimates (not company-confirmed) suggest like-for-like sales at existing stores fell around 4-6% in the April-June quarter and roughly 1.7% in the July-September quarter. The tension: the stock still trades at a very rich multiple built on the expectation that Zudio keeps scaling nationally, and that story is now being tested.
analysis.quarters: Q4 FY25 (reported April 2025) showed consolidated net profit falling 54.8% YoY - but this is not comparable: Q4 FY24 included a one-off ₹406 crore after-tax gain from an Ind AS 116 lease-term reassessment, so the decline is a base-effect artifact, not a business reversal. Q1 FY27 (June 2026) saw standalone revenue up roughly 18-19% YoY (sources show ₹5,666-5,755 crore) and profit up roughly 22-26% YoY (₹519-532 crore depending on source) - the stock still fell about 11% on the day because revenue growth missed street expectations and analysts flagged margin and like-for-like softness. The Q2 FY27 preliminary update (October 2026) showed growth re-accelerating to 23% YoY, with brokerage estimates of the like-for-like decline narrowing from roughly -4% to -6% in Q1 to about -1.7% in Q2 - management has not yet spoken to full Q2 numbers on an earnings call since results aren't out until 29 October.
analysis.performance_read: The uncomfortable fact first: the stock is down 63.8% from its all-time high of ₹8,218 (11 October 2024) to the current ₹2,971, and this is not a split or demerger artifact - the 2016 and 2026 stock splits appear to already be adjusted in this price series, so the fall is a genuine market re-rating, not a corporate-action illusion. Despite that, Trent has still beaten the Nifty and its closest listed peer, DMart (DMART), over 3 and 5 years (3Y: +41.3% vs Nifty +14.7% vs DMART -11.5%; 5Y: +158.5% vs Nifty +23.4% vs DMART -35.9%). Over 1 year, though, Trent has underperformed both (-35.6% vs Nifty -10.0% vs DMART -18.8%). This is a stock that ran up very hard on a growth narrative and has since given back a large chunk of that re-rating as growth decelerated, even while revenue and profit kept growing in absolute terms.
analysis.valuation_read: At a trailing P/E of roughly 86x and price-to-book of about 22.5x, Trent is still priced expensively even after a 64% fall from its peak - it was simply priced far more expensively before. That is why it is 'cheap' only relative to its own recent history, not cheap in any absolute sense versus the market or peers. The multiple still bakes in years of continued high-growth Zudio expansion; whether that is justified depends on whether the recent like-for-like softness is temporary (festive-season timing, new-store cannibalisation settling down) or a sign the growth rate is structurally slowing.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently store-count-led, not same-store-led: total revenue is up over 20% YoY largely because the store network keeps expanding (1,342 stores, Zudio past 1,000), while per-store sales appear to be shrinking on brokerage estimates. That is a weaker quality of growth than if both metrics were rising together, and it matters more for a business adding stores as fast as Trent is - new-store cannibalisation of nearby existing stores has been flagged by at least one broker as a specific drag on Zudio's market-share gains.
analysis.health_read: On paper, profitability and balance-sheet health look solid: ROE around 27.7% (28.6% on a 3-year average), ROCE around 28.3%, and a low debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.37. Promoter entity (Tata Sons) holds the bulk of the company debt-free with no pledging. Actual cash-conversion quality (operating cash flow vs reported profit) is not verified here - check on Screener. The real risk here reads as business risk (slowing like-for-like sales, margin pressure from Zudio's lower-ticket mix, cannibalisation) rather than financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 37.01% of Trent, with Tata Sons alone at 32.45% and Tata Investment Corporation also on the register; no promoter shares are pledged. Institutional ownership as of the June 2026 quarter: FIIs 15.14%, mutual funds 14.64%, DIIs 8.63%, others 24.58%. There is no widely-known individual marquee investor on the shareholding register for Trent - its ownership story is purely the Tata Group holding company structure, not a star-investor bet.
strengths: Store network reached 1,342 outlets by 30 September 2026, with Zudio crossing 1,000 stores in the quarter
H1 FY27 standalone revenue up 21% YoY to ₹11,454 crore, Q2 alone up 23% YoY
ROE ~27.7% and ROCE ~28.3%, with low leverage (debt-to-equity ~0.37) and no promoter pledge
Q2 FY27 preliminary data shows the like-for-like sales decline narrowing versus Q1 (brokerage estimates: roughly -1.7% vs -4% to -6%)
watchpoints: Like-for-like/same-store sales have been estimated negative for at least two consecutive quarters by brokerages (Nuvama, Goldman Sachs) - not yet confirmed by company disclosure
Revenue growth has decelerated over roughly six quarters before the Q2 FY27 preliminary uptick, and the stock fell 11% on the Q1 FY27 update alone
Margin pressure flagged by analysts from Zudio's lower average-ticket mix versus Westside, even though multi-year operating margin trend has been upward
Stock still trades at ~86x earnings and ~22.5x book despite a 64% fall from its October 2024 peak - a lot of future growth is still priced in
analysis.one_thing: The 29 October 2026 Q2/H1 FY27 results and management's commentary on like-for-like sales trends and margins - this will show whether the Q2 revenue re-acceleration and narrowing same-store decline (per preliminary data) is a genuine inflection or a one-quarter blip against the six-quarter slowdown.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked revenue/profit figures across Business Standard, Kotak Neo, Equitybulls and Multibagg; Q1 FY27 revenue (₹5,666 cr vs ₹5,755 cr) and profit (₹519 cr vs ₹532 cr) show minor discrepancies between sources - both ranges reported here rather than averaged. Like-for-like/SSSG decline figures (Q1 ~-4% to -6%, Q2 ~-1.7%) are brokerage estimates (Nuvama, Goldman Sachs), not company-disclosed numbers, and are flagged as such. P/E (~86x), P/B (~22.5x), ROE, ROCE and debt-to-equity are from screener.in and were not independently re-derived against the supplied last_close of ₹2,971. The Q4 FY25 profit-fall figure (-54.8%) is explained by a one-off Ind AS 116 lease-reassessment gain in the prior-year quarter and should not be read as an operating decline. Dividend yield (0.13% TTM) is negligible and not central to the investment case.
